concerns.concern: The linear-birefringence readout is not linear in the mode amplitudes. Its even-in-L dependence and a magnetoelastic δL·Q optical term could produce the rectification, SHG and DFG/SFG peaks from purely linear mode amplitudes, so the claimed intrinsic material nonlinearity is not established.
concerns.quote: The intrinsic (material) origin of the nonlinear signals is not established against readout (detection) nonlinearities.

concerns.concern: None of the existing controls can tell readout mixing from material mixing. Quadratic fluence scaling, the 2D peak coordinates and the S_AB − S_A − S_B subtraction all come out the same in both scenarios.
concerns.quote: The S_AB − S_A − S_B subtraction removes only terms linear in each pulse. It does not remove detection cross-terms.

concerns.concern: The DFG coherence disappears within about 30 ps while both parent modes persist beyond 100 ps. This needs a quantitative explanation, including phase and lifetime analysis against γ_Mag + γ_Ph3.
concerns.quote: Ext. Data Fig. 2 shows the DFG vanishing within about 30 ps while both parents persist beyond 100 ps, which requires quantitative explanation

concerns.concern: There is no probe-wavelength or probe-polarization dependence of the DFG-to-fundamental amplitude ratio. Such data would test whether the mixing is intrinsic to the material.
concerns.quote: probe-wavelength or probe-polarization dependence of the DFG/fundamental amplitude ratio (an intrinsic mode should be probe-independent up to its own optical coupling)

concerns.concern: The size of ΔLB relative to the static LB is not estimated, and the linearity of the balanced detector is not calibrated.
concerns.quote: an estimate of the size of ΔLB relative to static LB, and of the polarization-rotation linearity of the balanced detector

concerns.concern: There is no quantitative check that the DFG polarization pattern differs from the product of the magnon and Ph₃ patterns.
concerns.quote: a quantitative check that the DFG polarization pattern (Ext. Data Fig. 1c) differs from the product of the Mag and Ph₃ patterns

concerns.concern: The LB response to second order in δL and Q should be derived and its size compared with the measured DFG/SFG amplitudes. An independent probe (Faraday/Kerr at another wavelength, or THz emission) should confirm that the 0.45 THz coherence exists in the material.
concerns.quote: use an independent probe (e.g., Faraday/Kerr at a different wavelength, or THz emission) to confirm that the 0.45 THz coherence exists in the material

concerns.concern: The symmetry argument that second-order magnonic responses need magnon–phonon coupling is flawed. Longitudinal Néel-vector components, elliptical precession under C2/m symmetry and Holstein–Primakoff terms all give 0 and 2ω signals without DMI or phonons.
concerns.quote: the longitudinal component of the Néel vector, L_z ≈ L₀(1 − L_⊥²/2), contains 0 and 2ω components for any finite-amplitude precession.

concerns.concern: Because other mechanisms can produce magnon rectification and SHG, attributing these features to cascaded X_a²X_b terms is not a unique explanation.
concerns.quote: The paper's argument that cascaded X_a²X_b terms produce these features is not unique.

concerns.concern: The model treats the magnon doublet as a single mode. This conflicts with the observed Mag₊–Mag₋ DFG feature at 9 T, so the doublet structure and branch selection rules should enter the model.
concerns.quote: the 9 T data show a Mag₊–Mag₋ DFG feature, i.e., intra-doublet nonlinear mixing.

concerns.concern: No symmetry (irrep) analysis explains why only Ph₃ participates in three-wave mixing and not Ph₁, Ph₂ or Ph₅, even though Ph₁ and Ph₂ are also magnon-polaron partners.
concerns.quote: This is a central selection-rule question left unaddressed.

concerns.concern: The theoretical model omits quartic magnon terms and readout nonlinearities. The conclusion that X_a²X_b coupling dominates is therefore not robustly established.
concerns.quote: Hence the conclusion that "X_a²X_b is the dominant TWM mechanism" is not robustly established.

concerns.concern: The model's main discriminator, the absence of Ph₃ rectification, rests on a magnon-only detection operator. Experimentally, Ph₃ is clearly detected through LB.
concerns.quote: That conclusion depends on the assumed μ_det, which is "magnon-only", whereas experimentally Ph₃ is clearly detected through LB.

concerns.concern: Ph₃ SHG, which the competing X_b²X_a channel predicts, is observed experimentally. The paper attributes it post hoc to other phonon–phonon nonlinearities.
concerns.quote: Ph₃ SHG, which the X_b²X_a channel predicts, is observed experimentally but is attributed post hoc to other phonon–phonon nonlinearities.

concerns.concern: Agreement with experiment is weakly constraining, because the peak positions are fixed kinematically by the two mode frequencies and any cubic coupling would reproduce them.
concerns.quote: Peak positions are kinematically fixed by ω_Mag and ω_Ph3, so any cubic coupling reproduces them.

concerns.concern: The field-scaling fits are visual guides only: no log–log plots, free-exponent fits or uncertainties. The field range spans only a factor of about 1.6, so second and third order are hardly distinguishable.
concerns.quote: Over that range, n = 2 and n = 3, or a threshold behaviour, are hardly distinguishable

concerns.concern: In Fig. 1g the lowest-field points sit at zero. This is consistent with a noise floor or threshold rather than a clean power law.
concerns.quote: In Fig. 1g the lowest-field points sit at zero, consistent with a noise floor or threshold rather than a clean power law.

concerns.concern: At 9 T the THz field is at most 0.2 MV/cm, so quadratic scaling predicts roughly a 40-fold drop in DFG, yet the DFG peaks look comparably prominent to the 0 T data. This needs quantitative normalization, signal-to-noise numbers and an explanation.
concerns.quote: Yet the Mag±–Ph₃ DFG peaks in Fig. 3c appear with prominence comparable to the 0 T data.

concerns.concern: The driving field is H_THz, but E_THz is reported with different reference normalizations across figures, and no conversion to in-sample H (Fresnel, absorption) is given. This makes cross-figure comparison of nonlinear orders unreliable.
concerns.quote: The conversion to an in-sample H field (Fresnel factors, absorption in a 20 µm flake) is not given, so cross-figure comparison of orders is unreliable.

concerns.concern: The third-order NR, PP and R signals could come from cascaded second-order processes or intrinsic third-order terms. The manuscript does not separate these or show how they would scale differently.
concerns.quote: The manuscript does not separate the cascaded and intrinsic contributions, or show how they would scale differently (e.g., with sample thickness or detuning).

concerns.concern: The coupling parameters have inconsistent units with dimensionless quadratures. The conversion via ℓ is missing, β^a_bb and β^b_aa are compared across different units, and a Q_b/l factor is double-counted.
concerns.quote: The estimate β^a_bb ≈ 0.001 β^b_aa compares quantities with different units, and the extra "Q_b/l" factor is double-counted

concerns.concern: Key simulation parameters are not reported, so the modelling is not reproducible. Missing are g, μ_a, μ_det, κ, γ_φ, the pulse waveforms, the Fock-space truncation and the initial thermal state.
concerns.quote: The values of g, μ_a, μ_det, κ, γ_φ, the pulse waveforms, the Fock-space truncation and the initial (thermal) state are not reported.

concerns.concern: The simulated maps differ in absolute scale by about 10⁶, and there is no quantitative comparison of relative peak amplitudes with experiment.
concerns.quote: The simulated maps differ in absolute scale by about 10⁶ (×10⁻⁵ vs ×10⁻¹¹), and no quantitative comparison of peak ratios with experiment is attempted.

concerns.concern: The computed squeezing and entanglement are tiny and oscillate about zero, and thermal noise is neglected. The experiment measures only classical coherent amplitudes, with no access to quantum fluctuations.
concerns.quote: The computed effects are about −0.01 to −0.02 dB and E_N ≈ 0.006 (Ext. Data Fig. 7), oscillating about zero, with no thermal noise

concerns.concern: Claims such as "definitive" coherent TWM, entangling excitations, "hybrid quantum technologies" and the cavity-magnomechanics cooperativity analogy go well beyond what is demonstrated.
concerns.quote: phrases such as "entangle magnetic and vibrational excitations" and "hybrid quantum technologies", along with the cavity-magnomechanics analogy ("cooperativity of 15"), go well beyond what is demonstrated.

concerns.concern: Novelty, including the "first direct observation" claim, is not sharply delineated from prior work on THz-driven magnon polarons in FePS₃, photon-mediated coupling in CoF₂ and magnon-pair DFG in YFeO₃.
concerns.quote: Novelty relative to refs. 9, 34, 35, 46 (THz-driven magnon polarons and metastable magnetization in FePS₃; nonlinear magnon–phonon coupling in CoF₂) needs sharper delineation.

concerns.concern: The text says the linear field dependence of "infrared-active" modes rules out carrier effects, but elsewhere all observed modes are described as Raman-active. The exclusion argument and the description of how Ph₃ is driven need correcting.
concerns.quote: The logic of this exclusion argument should be corrected.

concerns.concern: The paper lacks a quantitative plot of DFG frequency versus ω_Mag − ω_Ph3 across temperature.
concerns.quote: Provide a quantitative plot of DFG frequency versus ω_Mag − ω_Ph3 across temperature (Fig. 1d).

concerns.concern: The complete peak-assignment table and data-processing details such as windowing and resolution should be included in the main or extended material.
concerns.quote: Include the complete peak-assignment table (Table S2) and the processing details (windowing, resolution) in the main or extended material.
